takeaways: The purpose of each link can be understood from its text alone, with no help from the sentence or card around it.
Level AAA. It is the stricter sibling of 2.4.4 (A), which also lets surrounding context explain a link.
The link text here means its accessible name, so a hidden longer name for a short visible link can count. Visible text that says it all is better for everyone.
Links whose purpose would be unclear to everyone, such as in a guessing game, are exempt.
failures: “Read more” that relies on the card title
“Here” in a sentence that explains where
check: List every link on the screen as plain text. Would each one make sense on a sticky note?
Look for any two links with the same text that go to different places.
Check that icon links have names that say where they lead, not what the icon looks like.

quiz.question: A report page lists six documents. Each row has the title, then a link that says “Download”. Under 2.4.9, what is the cleanest fix?
options: Keep “Download”; the row title explains it
Make the link text “Download annual report 2025 (PDF)”
quiz.why: At AAA the text alone must explain the link. The row title is context, which only 2.4.4 accepts, and the file size still does not say which document it is.

spec: Write link text that names the destination or action and the thing, like “View invoice 1042”.
Where the visible text must stay short, write the full accessible name and note it starts with the visible words.
Flag any repeated link labels in the file so they get unique names.
review: Out of context, does this link still say where it goes?
Is the hidden name consistent with what people see, so voice users can still say it?
Could we put this explanation in the visible link instead?
tradeoff: Fully descriptive links make dense lists and tables longer. Meeting 2.4.4 is the baseline; aim for 2.4.9 on content pages and lists of downloads, where descriptive links help everyone scan, and use hidden names sparingly elsewhere.
system: Give list, table and card components a link name field that defaults to the item title, so “View” or “Download” is never the whole name.
pitch: Clear link text is free to write and makes every page easier to scan. It is the cheapest AAA rule we can meet.
